question: What's the right CRM hygiene policy that reps actually follow?
answer:
**Weekly 30-minute Salesforce block time (during admin hours, not on call). One rule: Every open deal updated weekly with next action + expected close date. Enforcement: reps below 80% update rate lose territory allocation. Reward: transparent pipeline, no forecast surprises.** **Why most CRM policies fail:** - "Update Salesforce daily" → Takes 1 hour/day across team, reps resist. - "Update before forecast call" → Updates are Friday-night panic-coding, data is garbage. - No consequence for noncompliance → Rep ignores it, forecast call derails. **The policy that works:** 1. **Weekly cadence, not daily.** Every Monday 10–10:30 AM, CRM block time. Reps log in, they don't take calls. Why it works: reps know "1 meeting per week" vs. "always updating" feels reasonable. 2. **Minimum standard:** For every open opportunity >$10K: - **Next Action** (field): What's happening next? "Customer reviewing proposal," "Sent pricing," "Demo scheduled 4/15." No action = dead deal (aging rules kick in). - **Expected Close Date:** Realistic, not hopeful. If customer hasn't replied in 20 days and close date is next week, manager catches it Monday morning. - **Probability updated monthly, not weekly.** Moving it weekly encourages gaming. 3. **What you DON'T force:** - Call logging. (Gong captures calls; let it auto-sync.) - Activity count. (Doesn't correlate to revenue.) - Deal descriptions. (Waste of time if you have a good deal name.) - Custom fields with more than 2 dropdowns. (Reps hate them.) 4. **Enforcement:** - Dashboard: Reps sorted by "% of open deals updated in last 7 days." Top tier (>95%) gets priority on warm leads. Bottom tier (<80%) loses outbound list allocation. - Manager review: 5 min, weekly. "Joe, your negotiation deals are 40 days old with no next action. Call them today or move to closed/lost." - Consequence is real: territory realignment (Joe loses the $500K territory and works on expansion-only for a quarter). 5. **Tools to make it easy:** - Salesforce Mobile app (takes 30 seconds to add next action). - Slack integration for deal alerts ("Your deals over 30 days with no update:" @ each rep). - Formula field for "Days Since Last Activity" (auto-calc, easy to spot stale deals). **The script for manager coaching (5 min, weekly):** "Here's the CRM health report. Three things: 1. [Rep A], you're at 100%—keep it up, you're prioritized for new inbound. 2. [Rep B], you're at 70%—deal review Monday. Deals over 30 days stale move to closed-lost unless there's a real next step. 3. [Team], 'no next action' = dead deal. If customer hasn't responded in 20 days and you don't have a specific next action, close it or move it to nurture." **Benchmark (at 50 reps, $20M ARR):** | Target | Good | Concerning | |--------|------|----------| | % Deals Updated Weekly | >90% | <70% | | Avg Days in Stage | Sales cycle / 5 | Sales cycle / 2 | | Deals with No Action | <5% | >15% | **Action:** Pick one policy. Enforce it for 4 weeks. By week 3, reps will stop fighting it.
